output.brief: The Kestria buffering problem is almost certainly caused by the smart-TV app 5.2 release, not the new CDN. Kestria was the only market where 5.2 was switched on, starting 9 Oct, and it reached all Kestria TVs within about two days. In 12–25 Oct data, 5.2 sessions stalled 5.9% of the time. Every other client stalled 0.6–0.7%, including on the same ISPs and the same Tessaline CDN. Employee test TVs on the old CDN already showed 5.7% on 5.2 versus 0.6% on 5.1. The release lowered the startup buffer target, and that setting can be reverted per market within about an hour. Handball load and ISP congestion don't fit the data. Do not send the breach notice, withhold fees or move traffic back, and do not mute the alert. Instead, revert the Kestria setting to the 5.1 values, hold the 20 Nov wider rollout, and confirm that rebuffering and tickets fall. Add app version and device breakdowns to the dashboard. Hold off on the cancellation offer: the October price rise is a rival explanation for the cancellations, and buffering's share of them is unmeasured. I'm highly confident in the app cause.
